questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid cylinder having radius $R$ and length $L$ is slipping on a rough horizontal plane. At time $t=0$ the cylinder has a translational velocity $v_0=49$ m/s, perpendicular to its axis and a rotational velocity $v_0/4R$ about the centre. The time taken by the cylinder to start rolling is ________ seconds. (coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_K=0.25$ and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Initial translational velocity, $v_0 = 49$ m/s.

Initial angular velocity, $\omega_0 = \dfrac{v_0}{4R}$.

Velocity of the lowest point of the cylinder is $v_{bottom} = v_0 - \omega_0 R = v_0 - \dfrac{v_0}{4} = \dfrac{3v_0}{4} > 0$.

Since the lowest point is slipping forward, kinetic friction $f_k = \mu_k m g$ acts in the backward direction.

Translational acceleration, $a = -\dfrac{f_k}{m} = -\mu_k g$.

Angular acceleration, $\alpha = \dfrac{f_k R}{I} = \dfrac{\mu_k m g R}{\dfrac{1}{2} m R^2} = \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R}$.

At time $t$, the translational velocity is $v = v_0 - \mu_k g t$.

The angular velocity is $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = \dfrac{v_0}{4R} + \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R} t$.

For pure rolling to start, $v = \omega R$.

$v_0 - \mu_k g t = \left( \dfrac{v_0}{4R} + \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R} t \right) R$

$v_0 - \mu_k g t = \dfrac{v_0}{4} + 2\mu_k g t$

$3\mu_k g t = \dfrac{3v_0}{4}$

$t = \dfrac{v_0}{4\mu_k g}$

Substituting the given values $v_0 = 49$ m/s, $\mu_k = 0.25$, and $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$:

$t = \dfrac{49}{4 \times 0.25 \times 9.8} = \dfrac{49}{9.8} = 5$ s.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere ($A$) of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell ($B$) of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is __________.
questions.solution:
For a body of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolling without slipping under a force $F$ applied tangentially at the highest point, the torque about the point of contact with the ground is $\tau = F(2R)$.

The moment of inertia about the point of contact is $I = I_{cm} + MR^2$.

Using $\tau = I\alpha$ and the rolling without slipping condition $a = \alpha R$, we get:

$F(2R) = (I_{cm} + MR^2) \dfrac{a}{R} \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2FR^2}{I_{cm} + MR^2}$

For the solid sphere $A$ of mass $5m$:

$I_{cm,A} = \dfrac{2}{5}(5m)R^2 = 2mR^2$

$a_A = \dfrac{2FR^2}{2mR^2 + 5mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{7m}$

For the spherical shell $B$ of mass $m$:

$I_{cm,B} = \dfrac{2}{3}mR^2$

$a_B = \dfrac{2FR^2}{\dfrac{2}{3}mR^2 + mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{\dfrac{5}{3}m} = \dfrac{6F}{5m}$

The ratio of their accelerations is:

$\dfrac{a_A}{a_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2F}{7m}}{\dfrac{6F}{5m}} = \dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{5}{21}$

Answer: $5 : 21$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $4$ cm and mass $5$ kg is rotating (rotation axis is passing through the centre of the sphere) with an angular velocity of $1200$ rpm. It is brought to rest in $10$ s by applying a constant torque. The torque applied and the number of rotations it made before it comes to rest are _______ and _______ respectively.
questions.solution:
Initial angular velocity $\omega_0 = 1200 \text{ rpm} = \dfrac{1200 \times 2\pi}{60} = 40\pi \text{ rad/s}$

Final angular velocity $\omega = 0$

Time $t = 10 \text{ s}$

Angular acceleration $\alpha = \dfrac{\omega - \omega_0}{t} = \dfrac{0 - 40\pi}{10} = -4\pi \text{ rad/s}^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 5 \times (0.04)^2 = 0.0032 \text{ kg m}^2$

Torque $\tau = I|\alpha| = 0.0032 \times 4\pi = 0.0128\pi \text{ Nm}$

Angle rotated $\theta = \dfrac{\omega_0 + \omega}{2}t = \dfrac{40\pi + 0}{2} \times 10 = 200\pi \text{ rad}$

Number of rotations $N = \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{200\pi}{2\pi} = 100$

Answer: $0.0128\pi$ Nm, $100$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel initially at rest is subjected to a uniform angular acceleration about its axis. In the first $2\text{ s}$ it rotates through an angle $\theta_1$ and in the next $2\text{ s}$ it rotates through an angle $\theta_2$. The ratio $\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Using the equation of rotational kinematics $\theta = \omega_0 t + \dfrac{1}{2} \alpha t^2$.

Since the wheel is initially at rest, $\omega_0 = 0$.

Angle rotated in the first $2\text{ s}$:

$\theta_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \alpha (2)^2 = 2\alpha$

Angle rotated in the first $4\text{ s}$:

$\theta_{total} = \dfrac{1}{2} \alpha (4)^2 = 8\alpha$

Angle rotated in the next $2\text{ s}$:

$\theta_2 = \theta_{total} - \theta_1 = 8\alpha - 2\alpha = 6\alpha$

The ratio is:

$\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1} = \dfrac{6\alpha}{2\alpha} = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object of uniform density rolls up the curved path with the initial velocity $v_0$ as shown in the figure. If the maximum height attained by an object is $\dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}$ ($g$ = acceleration due to gravity), the object is a _______.
questions.solution:
By the law of conservation of mechanical energy, the total initial kinetic energy of the rolling object is converted into potential energy at the maximum height.

Total initial kinetic energy for an object rolling without slipping is given by:
$K = K_{\text{translational}} + K_{\text{rotational}}$
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

Substituting $\omega = \dfrac{v_0}{R}$ and $I = mk^2$ (where $k$ is the radius of gyration):
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}(mk^2)\left(\dfrac{v_0}{R}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2\left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$

The potential energy at the maximum height $h$ is:
$U = mgh$

Given $h = \dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}$, we have:
$U = mg\left(\dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}\right) = \dfrac{7}{10}mv_0^2$

Equating kinetic and potential energy ($K = U$):
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2\left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = \dfrac{7}{10}mv_0^2$

$1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{14}{10} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$\dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{7}{5} - 1 = \dfrac{2}{5}$

The moment of inertia is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2$, which corresponds to a solid sphere.

Answer: solid sphere

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is divided into two unequal parts. The smaller part having mass $M/8$ is converted into a sphere of radius $r$ and the larger part is converted into a circular disc of thickness $t$ and radius $2R$. If $I_1$ is moment of inertia of a sphere having radius $r$ about an axis through its centre and $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter, the ratio of their moment of inertia $I_2/I_1 = $ _____.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the original solid sphere be $M$ and its radius be $R$.

Mass of the smaller sphere, $m_1 = \dfrac{M}{8}$.
Since the material remains the same, the density is constant. The volume is directly proportional to the mass.
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{1}{8} \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\right) \Rightarrow r^3 = \dfrac{R^3}{8} \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{2}$

Moment of inertia of the smaller sphere about an axis through its centre is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5} m_1 r^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \left(\dfrac{M}{8}\right) \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{M}{8} \times \dfrac{R^2}{4} = \dfrac{M R^2}{80}$

Mass of the larger part (which is converted into a disc) is:
$m_2 = M - \dfrac{M}{8} = \dfrac{7M}{8}$

The radius of the disc is given as $2R$. The moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter is:
$I_2 = \dfrac{1}{4} m_2 (\text{radius})^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{7M}{8}\right) (2R)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{7M}{8} \times 4R^2 = \dfrac{7M R^2}{8}$

The ratio of their moments of inertia is:
$\dfrac{I_2}{I_1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{7M R^2}{8}}{\dfrac{M R^2}{80}} = \dfrac{7}{8} \times 80 = 70$

Answer: $70$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Moment of inertia about an axis $AB$ for a rod of mass $40$ kg and length $3$ m is same as that of a solid sphere of mass of $10$ kg and radius $R$ about an axis parallel to $AB$ axis with separation of $3$ m as shown in figure below. The value of $R$ is given as $\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{2}}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the rod about axis $AB$ passing through one of its ends:
$I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{ML^2}{3} = \dfrac{40 \times (3)^2}{3} = \dfrac{40 \times 9}{3} = 120\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the same axis $AB$, using the parallel axis theorem $I = I_{\text{cm}} + md^2$:
Mass $m = 10\text{ kg}$, radius $R$, distance from the centre of the sphere to axis $AB$ is $d = 3\text{ m}$.

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + md^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}(10)R^2 + 10(3)^2 = 4R^2 + 90$

Equating the two moments of inertia:
$120 = 4R^2 + 90$
$4R^2 = 30$
$R^2 = \dfrac{15}{2}$
$R = \sqrt{\dfrac{15}{2}}$

Comparing with $R = \sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{2}}$:
$\alpha = 15$

Hence, $\alpha = 15$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as $\theta = \dfrac{5t^4}{40} - \dfrac{t^3}{3}$. The angular acceleration of the particle after $10$ seconds is _______ rad/s$^2$.
questions.solution:
Given $\theta = \dfrac{5t^4}{40} - \dfrac{t^3}{3} = \dfrac{t^4}{8} - \dfrac{t^3}{3}$

Angular velocity $\omega = \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = \dfrac{4t^3}{8} - \dfrac{3t^2}{3} = \dfrac{t^3}{2} - t^2$

Angular acceleration $\alpha = \dfrac{d\omega}{dt} = \dfrac{3t^2}{2} - 2t$

At $t = 10$ s, $\alpha = \dfrac{3(10)^2}{2} - 2(10)$

$\alpha = 150 - 20 = 130$ rad/s$^2$

Answer: $130$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the position vector $\vec{r}=x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}$ changes sign as $-\vec{r}$, which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change ?
questions.solution:
The transformation $\vec{r} \to -\vec{r}$ is known as a parity transformation (inversion through the origin).
Vectors that change sign under parity are called polar vectors, while those that do not change sign are called axial vectors (or pseudovectors).
Velocity is defined as $\vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}$. Since $\vec{r} \to -\vec{r}$, we have $\vec{v} \to -\vec{v}$.
Acceleration is defined as $\vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}$. Since $\vec{v} \to -\vec{v}$, we have $\vec{a} \to -\vec{a}$.
Linear momentum is defined as $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$. Since $\vec{v} \to -\vec{v}$, we have $\vec{p} \to -\vec{p}$.
Angular momentum is defined as $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$.
Under the transformation $\vec{r} \to -\vec{r}$ and $\vec{p} \to -\vec{p}$, the cross product becomes:
$\vec{L}' = (-\vec{r}) \times (-\vec{p}) = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = \vec{L}$.
Thus, angular momentum does not flip its sign under the transformation $\vec{r} \to -\vec{r}$.

Thus, angular momentum does not flip its sign under the transformation $\vec{r} \to -\vec{r}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{J}.\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the flywheel be $M = 3$ kg and its radius be $R = 5$ m.
Let the hanging mass be $m = 3$ kg and the distance descended be $h = 3$ m.
The flywheel is a disk, so its moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
By conservation of energy, the loss in potential energy of the hanging mass equals the gain in kinetic energy of the system.
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$
Since the string does not slip, $v = R\omega$, so $\omega = \frac{v}{R}$.
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}MR^2)(\frac{v}{R})^2$
$mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{4}Mv^2$
Substituting the values: $3 \times 10 \times 3 = \frac{1}{2}(3)v^2 + \frac{1}{4}(3)v^2$
$90 = \frac{3}{2}v^2 + \frac{3}{4}v^2 = \frac{9}{4}v^2$
$v^2 = \frac{90 \times 4}{9} = 40$ m$^2$/s$^2$.
The kinetic energy of the wheel is $K_{wheel} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{4}Mv^2$.
$K_{wheel} = \frac{1}{4} \times 3 \times 40 = 30$ J.

If the mass of each disc is 600 gm and applied torque between two discs is $43 \times 10^{5}$ dyne. cm, the angular acceleration of the discs about the given axis $A B$ is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is $\sqrt{n} \mathrm{~cm}$. The value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
Using the parallel axis theorem for radius of gyration:
$k^2 = k_{cm}^2 + d^2$ where $k_{cm}$ is the radius of gyration about the center of mass and $d$ is the distance from the center.
For a solid sphere:
$I_{center} = \frac{2}{5}MR^2$, so $k_{cm}^2 = \frac{2}{5}R^2$
With $R = 10$ cm and $d = 15$ cm:
$k^2 = \frac{2}{5}(10)^2 + (15)^2 = 40 + 225 = 265$
Since $k = \sqrt{n}$, we have $n = 265$.

questions.q: A thin uniform rod $(X)$ of mass $M$ and length $L$ is pivoted at a height $\left(\frac{L}{3}\right)$ as shown in the figure. The rod is allowed to fall from a vertical position and lie horizontally on the table. The angular velocity of this rod when it hits the table top, is $\_\_\_\_$. ($\mathrm{g}=$ gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
The rod is pivoted at a distance $\frac{L}{3}$ from one end. The centre of mass is at a distance $\frac{L}{6}$ from the pivot.
Using energy conservation:
$mg\frac{\ell}{6} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$
Moment of inertia about the pivot (using parallel axis theorem):
$I = \frac{m\ell^2}{12} + m\left(\frac{\ell}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{m\ell^2}{12} + \frac{m\ell^2}{36} = \frac{m\ell^2}{9}$
$mg\frac{\ell}{6} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{m\ell^2}{9} \cdot \omega^2$
$\omega^2 = \frac{9g}{6 \cdot \frac{\ell}{2}} = \frac{3g}{\ell}$
$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{3g}{\ell}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder of length $L$ and radius $R$ has moment of inertia about its axis equal to $I_{1}$. A small co-centric cylinder of length $L / 2$ and radius $R / 3$ carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to $I_{2}$. The ratio $I_{1} / I_{2}$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For solid cylinder: $I = \frac{1}{2}mR^2$
Large cylinder: mass $m_1 = \rho \pi R^2 L$, so $I_1 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^2 L \times R^2 = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L}{2}$
Small cylinder (carved out): length L/2, radius R/3, mass $m_2 = \rho \pi(R/3)^2(L/2) = \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18}$
$I_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18} \times (R/3)^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18} \times \frac{R^2}{9} = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L}{324}$
$\frac{I_1}{I_2} = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L/2}{\rho \pi R^4 L/324} = \frac{324}{2} = 162$

questions.q: Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest the heavier mass is observed to fall 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is $\_\_\_\_ \mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{m}^{2}$. $\left(\mathrm{g}=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
From kinematics with $s = 0.81$ m and $t = 9$ s: $a = 2s/t^2 = 0.02$ m/s².
For the pulley system, applying Newton's second law to both masses and torque equation: $(m_1 - m_2)g - (m_1 + m_2)a = Ia/R^2$.
Substituting values: $0.05 \times 9.8 - 0.75 \times 0.02 = I \times 50$ gives $0.49 - 0.015 = 50I$.
Therefore $I = 9.5 \times 10^{-3}$ kg·m²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass $M \mathrm{~kg}$ and radius $r \mathrm{~m}$ shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis $A$ of the disc is given by $\frac{x}{256} M r^{2}$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of the complete disc about axis A is
$I_{disc} = \frac{1}{2}Mr^2 = \frac{128Mr^2}{256}$.
Each removed circular region has radius $r/4$ and mass $m_i = M/(r^2/16r^2) = M/16$.
For each removed disc at distance $3r/4$ from axis A, using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_{removed} = \frac{1}{2}m_i(r/4)^2 + m_i(3r/4)^2 = \frac{Mr^2}{512} + \frac{9Mr^2}{256} = \frac{19Mr^2}{512}$.
For two removed discs:
$I_{2removed} = \frac{38Mr^2}{512} = \frac{19Mr^2}{256}$.
Therefore:
$I_{remainder} = \frac{128Mr^2}{256} - \frac{19Mr^2}{256} = \frac{109Mr^2}{256}$, so $x = 109$.

questions.q: Two small balls with masses $m$ and 2 m are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length $d$ and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is $L$ about an axis ($A$) passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about $A$ is :
questions.solution:
CM from mass $m$: $x_{cm} = \frac{2md}{3m} = \frac{2d}{3}$.
Distances: $m$ is $2d/3$ from CM, $2m$ is $d/3$ from CM.
$I_{cm} = m(2d/3)^2 + 2m(d/3)^2 = \frac{4md^2}{9} + \frac{2md^2}{9} = \frac{2md^2}{3}$.
$L = I\omega \Rightarrow \omega = \frac{L}{I} = \frac{3L}{2md^2}$.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius $R$ and length $L(\mathrm{R}<\mathrm{L})$ about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as $M$) :
questions.solution:
Each cylinder has mass $M/4$, radius $R$, length $L$.
Axis through midpoints of top and bottom sides (along y-direction).
Top/bottom cylinders (perpendicular to axis, axis through midpoint):
$I = \frac{M_c R^2}{4} + \frac{M_c L^2}{12}$ each.
Left/right cylinders (parallel to axis, distance $L/2$ from it):
$I = \frac{M_c R^2}{2} + M_c(L/2)^2$ each.
Total $= 2\left(\frac{M_c R^2}{4}+\frac{M_c L^2}{12}\right) + 2\left(\frac{M_c R^2}{2}+\frac{M_c L^2}{4}\right)$
$= \frac{M}{2}\left(\frac{3R^2}{4}+\frac{L^2}{3}\right) = \frac{3MR^2}{8}+\frac{ML^2}{6}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform bar of length 12 cm and mass $20 m$ lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses $m$ and $2 m$ are moving in opposite directions with same speed of $v$ and in the same plane as the bar, as shown in figure. These masses strike the bar simultaneously and get stuck to it. After collision the entire system is rotating with angular frequency $\omega$. The ratio of $v$ and $\omega$ is :
questions.solution:
Linear momentum conservation: $mv - 2mv = 23m \cdot v_{cm}$, giving $v_{cm} = -\frac{v}{23}$.
Angular momentum about center of mass from the collision geometry:
Taking collision points 2 cm and 4 cm from the 12 cm bar's center at different positions, the angular momentum is $L = m \cdot v \cdot r_1 + (-2m) \cdot v \cdot r_2$.
Calculating moment of inertia: $I = \frac{1}{12}(20m)(0.12)^2 + m(0.02)^2 + 2m(0.04)^2 = 0.0276m$
The angular frequency $\omega$ is obtained from $\omega = \frac{L}{I}$, giving ratio $\frac{v}{\omega} = 33$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two masses $m$ and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius $r=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. (Assume string does not slip and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the masses be $v$ and the angular velocity of the pulley be $\omega = v/r$ since the string does not slip.
The pulley is a disc of mass $M = 30m$ and radius $r$. Its moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}Mr^2 = \frac{1}{2}(30m)r^2 = 15mr^2$.
Using the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the loss in potential energy of the system equals the gain in kinetic energy.
When the mass $2m$ descends by $h = 3.6$ m, the mass $m$ ascends by $h = 3.6$ m.
Loss in potential energy $\Delta U = (2m)gh - (m)gh = mgh$.
Gain in kinetic energy $\Delta K = \frac{1}{2}(2m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}(m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.
Substituting $I$ and $\omega$: $\Delta K = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}(15mr^2)(\frac{v}{r})^2 = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{15}{2}mv^2 = 9mv^2$.
Equating $\Delta U = \Delta K$: $mgh = 9mv^2$.
$v^2 = \frac{gh}{9}$.
Given $g = 10$ m/s$^2$ and $h = 3.6$ m:
$v^2 = \frac{10 \times 3.6}{9} = \frac{36}{9} = 4$.
$v = \sqrt{4} = 2$ m/s.

questions.q: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{kg}. \mathrm{m}^{2}$.
questions.solution:
For two solid spheres in contact with the tangent line at the contact point.
Sphere 1: $m_1 = 5$ kg, $r_1 = 0.1$ m
Sphere 2: $m_2 = 10$ kg, $r_2 = 0.2$ m
For a solid sphere, $I_{cm} = \frac{2}{5}mr^2$
The tangent at contact is perpendicular to the line joining centers. The perpendicular distance from each sphere's center to this tangent line equals its radius.
Using parallel axis theorem: $I_{total} = I_{cm} + md^2$
For sphere 1: $I_1 = \frac{2}{5}(5)(0.1)^2 + 5(0.1)^2 = 0.02 + 0.05 = 0.07$ kg·m²
For sphere 2: $I_2 = \frac{2}{5}(10)(0.2)^2 + 10(0.2)^2 = 0.16 + 0.4 = 0.56$ kg·m²
Total: $I = 0.07 + 0.56 = 0.63$ kg·m²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular disc has radius $R_{1}$ and thickness $T_{1}$. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius $R_{2}$ and thickness $T_{2}$. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and $\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=2$ then $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{1}{\alpha}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For a circular disc made of material with density $\rho$, moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^2 T \cdot R^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^4 T$.
For disc 1: $I_1 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R_1^4 T_1$
For disc 2: $I_2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R_2^4 T_2$
Given $I_1 = I_2$:
$R_1^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
With $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = 2$:
$(2R_2)^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
$16 R_2^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
$\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{1}{16}$
Therefore $\alpha = 16$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of $M$. Two blocks of mass of $M$ and $m$ are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is $\_\_\_\_$ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.solution:
The pulley consists of a rim (mass $M$) and two rods (each mass $M$) forming a diameter structure.
The moment of inertia is: $I = I_{rim} + I_{rods} = MR^2 + 2 \times \frac{MR^2}{3} = \frac{5MR^2}{3}$.
For the Atwood pulley system, applying Newton's second law:
Mass $m$ (upward): $T_1 = m(g-a)$
Mass $M$ (downward): $T_2 = M(g+a)$
Pulley rotation: $T_2 R - T_1 R = I\alpha = \frac{5MR^2}{3} \cdot \frac{a}{R}$
Thus: $T_2 - T_1 = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
Substituting: $M(g+a) - m(g-a) = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
$(M-m)g + (M+m)a = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
$(M-m)g = a\left(\frac{5M}{3} - M - m\right) = a\left(\frac{2M}{3} - m\right)$
$a = \frac{(M-m)g}{\frac{2M-3m}{3}} = \frac{3(M-m)g}{2M+3m}$, which is option (2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two cars $A$ and $B$ each of mass $10^{3} \mathrm{~kg}$ are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m, in same direction with speeds $72 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ and $36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. The magnitude of angular momentum of $\operatorname{car} A$ with respect to $\operatorname{car} B$ is $\_\_\_\_$ J.s.
questions.solution:
Mass of each car $m = 10^3$ kg.
Speed of car $A$, $v_A = 72$ km/h $= 72 \times \frac{5}{18} = 20$ m/s.
Speed of car $B$, $v_B = 36$ km/h $= 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10$ m/s.
Relative velocity of car $A$ with respect to car $B$ is $v_{AB} = v_A - v_B = 20 - 10 = 10$ m/s.
The cars are moving on parallel tracks separated by a perpendicular distance $d = 10$ m.
The magnitude of angular momentum of car $A$ with respect to car $B$ is given by $L = m \times v_{AB} \times d$.
Substituting the values: $L = 10^3 \times 10 \times 10 = 10^5$ J.s.
Thus, the correct option is (2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rod of mass $m$ and length $l$ suspended by means of two identical inextensible light strings as shown in figure. Tension in one string immediately after the other string is cut, is $\_\_\_\_$. $(g$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
When string at B is cut, rod rotates about A.
Torque about A: $\tau = mg \times \frac{l}{2}$
Moment of inertia about A: $I_A = \frac{ml^2}{3}$
Angular acceleration: $\alpha = \frac{mg \cdot l/2}{ml^2/3} = \frac{3g}{2l}$
Acceleration of COM: $a_{cm} = \alpha \times \frac{l}{2} = \frac{3g}{4}$
Newton's second law: $mg - T = ma_{cm}$
$T = mg - \frac{3mg}{4} = \frac{mg}{4}$

questions.q: Two identical thin rods of mass $M \mathrm{~kg}$ and length $L \mathrm{~m}$ are connected as shown in figure. Moment of inertia of the combined rod system about an axis passing through point $P$ and perpendicular to the plane of the rods is $\frac{x}{12} \mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{2}$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For vertical rod with axis at end P: $I_1 = \frac{ML^2}{3}$
For horizontal rod centered at distance L from P:
$I_2 = \int_{-L/2}^{L/2} \frac{M}{L}(x^2 + L^2)dx = \frac{M}{L}\left[\frac{x^3}{3} + L^2x\right]_{-L/2}^{L/2}$
$= \frac{M}{L}\left[\frac{L^3}{12} + L^3\right] = \frac{13ML^2}{12}$
Total: $I = \frac{ML^2}{3} + \frac{13ML^2}{12} = \frac{4ML^2 + 13ML^2}{12} = \frac{17ML^2}{12}$
$x = 17$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin solid disk of 1 kg is rotating along its diameter axis at the speed of 1800 rpm. By applying an external torque of $25 \pi \mathrm{Nm}$ for 40 s, the speed increases to 2100 rpm. The diameter of the disk is ________ m.
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{m}=1 \mathrm{~kg}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \omega_{\mathrm{i}}=1800 \mathrm{rpm}=1800 \times \frac{2 \pi}{60}=60 \pi \frac{\mathrm{rad}}{\mathrm{sec}} \\ & \omega_{\mathrm{f}}=2100 \mathrm{rpm}=2100 \times \frac{2 \pi}{60}=70 \pi \frac{\mathrm{rad}}{\mathrm{sec}} \\ & \tau_{e x t}=25 \pi \mathrm{Nm} \\ & \mathrm{t}=40 \mathrm{sec}
\end{aligned}$
Using equation of motion
$\begin{aligned}
& \omega_{\mathrm{f}}=\omega_{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \mathrm{t} \\ & 70 \pi=60 \pi+\alpha(40) \\ & \alpha=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}^2
\end{aligned}$
Also, $\tau=\mathrm{I} \alpha$
$\tau=\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{4} \alpha$
$\begin{aligned}
& 25 \pi=\frac{1 \times \mathrm{R}^2}{4} \times \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \mathrm{R}=20 \mathrm{~m}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, diameter of disk $=2 \mathrm{R}=2 \times 20=40 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q:
A cube having a side of 10 cm with unknown mass and 200 gm mass were hung at two ends of an uniform rigid rod of 27 cm long. The rod along with masses was placed on a wedge keeping the distance between wedge point and 200 gm weight as 25 cm. Initially the masses were not at balance. A beaker is placed beneath the unknown mass and water is added slowly to it. At given point the masses were in balance and half volume of the unknown mass was inside the water.
(Take the density of unknown mass is more than that of the water, the mass did not absorb water and water density is $1 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^3$.) The unknown mass is ________ kg.
questions.solution:
Given, volume of block $=\left(10 \times 10^{-2}\right)^3=10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^3$
Let density of block $=\rho \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$
mass of block $=\rho \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg}$
Buoyant Force $\left(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}\right)=1000 \times \frac{10^{-3}}{2} \times 10=5 \mathrm{~N}$
F.B.D. of blocks
Balancing torque about point O , we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{mg}\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)=0.2 \mathrm{~g}\left(25 \times 10^{-2}\right) \\ & \rho \times 10^{-3} \times 10 \times 2-10=50 \\ & \rho=3000 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3
\end{aligned}$
Hence, mass of block $=\rho \times 10^{-3}$
$=3000 \times 10^{-3}=3 \mathrm{~kg}$

\end{aligned}$
$\omega_2=32 \omega_1$ value of x is 32

$\omega_2=32 \omega_1$ value of x is 32
Answer is 32

A circular disk of radius R meter and mass M kg is rotating around the axis perpendicular to the disk. An external torque is applied to the disk such that $\theta(t)=5 t^2-8 t$, where $\theta(t)$ is the angular position of the rotating disc as a function of time $t$.
How much power is delivered by the applied torque, when $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ ?
questions.explanation:
$\begin{aligned}
& \theta=5 \mathrm{t}^2-8 \mathrm{t} \\
& \omega=\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \mathrm{t}-8 \\
& \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{p}=\tau \omega \\
& =(\mathrm{I} \alpha) \omega \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{2}\right) \alpha \omega \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{2}\right)(10)(10
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The torque due to the force $(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+2 \hat{k})$ about the origin, acting on a particle whose position vector is $(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$, would be

questions.q: A uniform circular disc of radius ' R ' and mass ' M ' is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_{\text{complete }}=\frac{M R^2}{2} \\ & \begin{aligned} I_{\text{removed }} & =\left(\frac{M}{4}\right)\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 \frac{1}{2}+\left(\frac{M}{4}\right)\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{3 M R^2}{32} \\ I=\frac{M R^2}{2} & -\frac{3 M R^2}{32}=\frac{13}{32} M R^2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The position vectors of two 1 kg particles, (A) and (B), are given by
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{A}}=\left(\alpha_1 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{i}+\alpha_2 \mathrm{t} \hat{j}+\alpha_3 \mathrm{t} \hat{k}\right) \mathrm{m}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{B}}=\left(\beta_1 \mathrm{t} \hat{i}+\beta_2 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{j}+\beta_3 \mathrm{t} \hat{k}\right) \mathrm{m}$, respectively; $\left(\alpha_1=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \alpha_2=3 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}, \alpha_3=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \beta_1=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \beta_2=-1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \beta_3=4 \mathrm{pm} / \mathrm{s}\right)$, where t is time, n and p are constants. At $t=1 \mathrm{~s},\left|\overrightarrow{V_A}\right|=\left|\vec{V}_B\right|$ and velocities $\vec{V}_A and \vec{V}_B$ of the particles are orthogonal to each other. At $t=1 \mathrm{~s}, the magnitude of angular momentum of particle (A) with respect to the position of particle (B) is $\sqrt{$\mathrm{L}}\mathrm{kgm}^2\mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The value of L is _______ .
questions.solution:
At $t=1 r_{A B}=-1 \hat{i}+(3 n+1) \hat{j}+(2-4 p) \hat{k}$

At $t=1 \begin{aligned}
& v_A=2 \hat{i}+3 n \hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\
& v_B=2 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+4 p \hat{k} \\
& \vec{v}_A-\vec{v}_B=0, \quad 4-6 n+8 p=0
\end{aligned} \begin{gathered}\left|v_A\right|=\left|v_B\right| \quad(3 n)^2+4=4+16 p^2 \\ 3 n=-4 p \\ 4+16 p=0 \\ p=-\frac{1}{4}, n=\frac{1}{3} \\ r_{A B}=-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k} \\ v_A=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\ \therefore L=m\left|\vec{r}_{A B} \times \vec{v}_A\right|=90\end{gathered}$

questions.q: A circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length $l$. When it slips down the plane, if takes $t \mathrm{~s}$. When it rolls down the plane then it takes $\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{1 / 2} t \mathrm{~s}$, where $\alpha$ is _________
questions.solution:
For slipping
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta \\
& \ell=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}}\end{aligned}$
For rolling
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{a}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}{1+\frac{\mathrm{k}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}}\left[\mathrm{k}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}^{\prime}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}{3} \\& \ell=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a}^{\prime}\left(\mathrm{t}^{\prime}\right)^2 \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}^{\prime}=\sqrt{\frac{6 \ell}{2 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}}=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2}} \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha=3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the radius of earth is reduced to three-fourth of its present value without change in its mass then value of duration of the day of earth will be ______ hours 30 minutes.
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2 \\
& \left(\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{MR}^2\right) \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_1}=\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{M}\left(\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{R}\right)^2 \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_1}=\frac{9}{16 \mathrm{~T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{9}{16} \times \mathrm{T}_1=\frac{9}{16} \times 24 \mathrm{hr}=\frac{27}{2} \mathrm{hr}=13 \mathrm{hr} 30 \mathrm{mins} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A ball of mass $0 . 5kg$ is attached to a string of length $50cm$. The ball is rotated on a horizontal circular path about its vertical axis. The maximum tension that the string can bear is $400N$. The maximum possible value of angular velocity of the ball in $rad{s}^{- 1}$ is,:
questions.solution:
Let the string makes angle $\theta$ with the vertical. Weight will be balanced by the vertical component of tension, which is $Tcos\theta = mg$ and the horizontal component towards the centre will provide the required centripetal force for circular motion. Therefore,

$Tsin\theta = m{\omega}^{2}\left(lsin\theta\right)$, where $l =$length of the string.

$⇒ 400sin\theta = 0 .5 {\omega}^{2} \times 0 .5 sin\theta$

$⇒ \omega = 40rad{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two discs of moment of inertia ${I}_{1} = 4kg{m}^{2}$ and ${I}_{2} = 2kg{m}^{2}$ about their central axes & normal to their planes, rotating with angular speeds $10rad{s}^{- 1} \text{ and } 4rad{s}^{- 1}$ respectively are brought into contact face to face with their axe of rotation coincident. The loss in kinetic energy of the system in the process is _________$J$.
questions.solution:
Applying conservation of angular momentum, we get

${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} + {I}_{2}{\omega}_{2} = \left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right){\omega}_{0} ⇒ 4 \times 10 + 2 \times 4 = \left(4 + 2\right){\omega}_{0} ⇒ {\omega}_{0} = 8rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, initial rotational kinetic energy is ${E}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{2}{\omega}_{2}^{2} = 216J$

and final rotational kinetic energy is

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right){\omega}_{0}^{2} = 192J$

Required, energy loss $\DeltaE = {E}_{1} - {E}_{2} = 24J$

questions.q: Consider a disc of mass $5kg$, radius $2m$, rotating with angular velocity of $10rad{s}^{- 1}$ about an axis perpendicular to the plane of rotation. An identical disc is kept gently over the rotating disc along the same axis. The energy dissipated so that both the discs continue to rotate together without slipping is _________$J$.
questions.solution:
Initial angular momentum, ${L}_{i} = I{\omega}_{i} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} \cdot \omega = 100kg{m}^{2}{s}^{- 1}$

Initial kinetic energy, ${E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} \cdot {\omega}^{2} = 500J$

From conservation of angular momentum, we can write

$\overset{\to}{L}i = \overset{\to}{L}f ⇒ 100 = 2I{\omega}_{f}$

$⇒ {\omega}_{f} = 5rad{s}^{- 1}$

${E}_{f} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{5 ( 2{)}^{2}}{2} \cdot ( 5{)}^{2} = 250J$

Therefore, required energy loss $\DeltaE = 250J$

questions.q: A cylinder is rolling down on an inclined plane of inclination $60 °$. Its acceleration during rolling down will be $\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}m{s}^{- 2}$, where $x =$ _______(use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$).
questions.solution:
For rolling motion, the acceleration of the cylinder along the inclined plane can be expressed as

$a = \dfrac{gsin\theta}{1 + \dfrac{{I}_{cm}}{M{R}^{2}}} . . . \left(1\right)$

The moment of inertia of the cylinder can be written as

${I}_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it follows that

$\begin{cases}a & = & \dfrac{gsin\theta}{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}} \\ & = & \dfrac{2 \times 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{3} \\ & = & \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{3}}m{s}^{- 2}\end{cases}$

Therefore, $x = 10$.

questions.q: A ring and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of both bodies are identical and the ratio of their kinetic energies is $\dfrac{7}{x}$, where $x$ is ______.

In pure rolling work done by friction is zero. Hence, potential energy is converted into kinetic energy. Since initially the ring and the sphere have same potential energy, finally they will have same kinetic energy too.

$⇒ \dfrac{7}{x} = 1 ⇒ x = 7$

For the equilibrium of the system, the net torque, according to the above figure, on the system about point $A$ should be zero.

${F}_{2} = 3kg - wt$

questions.q: Four particles, each of mass $1kg$ are placed at four corners of a square of side $2m$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is $______kg{m}^{2}$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the moment of inertia of a system of particles about a point can be written as

$I = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{m}_{i}{r}_{i}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, ${m}_{i}$ is the mass of the ${i}^{th}$ particle situated at a distance ${r}_{i}$ from the point.

With reference to the above diagram, it can be written that the net moment of inertia of the system of particles is

$\begin{cases}I & = & m{a}^{2} + m{a}^{2} + m ( \sqrt{2}a{)}^{2} \\ & = & 4m{a}^{2} \\ & = & 4 \times 1kg \times {\left(2m\right)}^{2} \\ & = & 16kg{m}^{2}\end{cases}$

$τ = Fr . . . $\left(2\right)$

$\begin{cases}\alpha & = & $\dfrac{52 . 5N}{5kg \times 0 . 70m}$ \\ & = & 15rad{s}^{- 2}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: For rolling spherical shell, the ratio of rotational kinetic energy and total kinetic energy is $\dfrac{x}{5}$. The value of $x$ is _____.

The rotational kinetic energy is given by

${K}_{tot} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{6}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2}$

Thus, the ratio is

$\overset{\to}{r} = ( 0 - 2 ) \overset{^}{i} + ( 0 + 3 ) \overset{^}{j} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F} = ( - 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} ) \times ( - P\overset{^}{k} )$

questions.solution:
Given here,

Moment of inertia of a disc of mass $M$ and radius '$R$' about any of its diameter is $\dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4}$.

questions.q: A solid cylinder is released from rest from the top of an inclined plane of inclination $30 °$ and length $60cm$. If the cylinder rolls without slipping, its speed upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane is ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$. (Given $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Let speed of cylinder upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane be $v$.

Here, gain in kinetic energy$=$loss in potential energy

So, $\dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{r}^{2}}{2}\right){\omega}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 °$

For pure rolling, $v = r\omega$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{r}^{2}}{2}\right){\left(\dfrac{v}{r}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 °$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 ° ⇒ \dfrac{3}{4}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{mgl}{2} ⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4gl}{6}}$

Putting the values, we have

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 10 \times 0 . 6}{6}} = 2m{s}^{- 1}$

The densities of materials are in the ratio $3: 5$. The moment of inertia of these discs respectively about their diameters will be in the ratio of $\dfrac{x}{6}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Mass of the disc in terms of density can be written as, $m = ρ\left(\pi{R}^{2}t\right)$.

$⇒ {R}^{2} = \dfrac{m}{ρ\pit}$

Now moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is, $\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{4}$.

Therefore,

$I = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{{m}^{2}}{4ρ\pit} ⇒ I ∝ \dfrac{1}{ρt}$

Required ratio, $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{2}{t}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1}{t}_{1}} = \dfrac{5}{3} \times \dfrac{0 . 5}{1} = \dfrac{5}{6}$

Hence, $x = 5$.

questions.solution:
Let velocity of centre of mass of sphere be $v$.

Total kinetic energy of solid sphere is $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$, where, $I$ is moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the axis passing through it's centre of mass and $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}\left(\text{pure rolling condition}\right)$.

Therefore,

$7 \times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times ( v{)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{5} ( 1 ) {R}^{2}\right]{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{v}^{2}\left(\dfrac{7}{5}\right) = 7 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ v = {10}^{- 1} = 0 . 1m{s}^{- 1} = 10cm{s}^{- 1}$

Acceleration of the disc, $a = - {\mu}_{k}g = - 3m{s}^{- 2}$.

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about any diameter is given by, $\dfrac{2{m}_{1}{R}^{2}}{5}$.

Using parallel axis theorem, we get

${I}_{\text{solid sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}{m}_{1}{R}^{2} + {m}_{1}{R}^{2} = \dfrac{7}{5}{m}_{1}{R}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{7}{5} \times 5{R}^{2}$

$= 7{R}^{2}$

Moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is given by, $\dfrac{{m}_{2}{R}^{2}}{4}$.

${I}_{\text{disc}} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}{R}^{2}}{4} + {m}_{2}{R}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}{m}_{2}{R}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{5}{4} \times 4{R}^{2}$

$= 5{R}^{2}$

Therefore,$\dfrac{{I}_{\text{disc}}}{{I}_{\text{soild sphere}}} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

Thus, $x = 5$.

questions.solution:
We have, ${I}_{CM} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}$

Since $AB$ is parallel to diameter and at a distance of $\dfrac{2}{3}R$ from it, using parallel axis theorem,

${I}_{AB} = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2} + m{\left(\dfrac{2R}{3}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{17}{18}m{R}^{2}$

Thus, the ratio is

$∴ \dfrac{{I}_{AB}}{{I}_{CM}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{17}{18}M{R}^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{17}{9}$

Thus, $x = 17$

questions.q:
A uniform solid cylinder with radius $R$ and length $L$ has moment of inertia ${I}_{1}$, about the axis of cylinder. A concentric solid cylinder of radius ${R}^{'} = \dfrac{R}{2}$ and length ${L}^{'} = \dfrac{L}{2}$ is carved out of the original cylinder. If ${I}_{2}$ is the moment of inertia of the carved out portion of the cylinder then $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} =$ __________.

(Both ${I}_{1}$ and ${I}_{2}$ are about the axis of the cylinder)
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ about the axis is ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{{M}_{1}{R}^{2}}{2}$.

Moment of inertia of carved out portion of the cylinder of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and length $\dfrac{L}{2}$ is ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{{M}_{2}{\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{{M}_{2}{R}^{2}}{8}$

Now, the ratio $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{4{M}_{1}}{{M}_{2}}$

As, $mass = density \times volume$

So, $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{4 \times ρ\pi{R}^{2}L}{\dfrac{ρ\pi{R}^{2}L}{4 \times 2}} = 32$

Using parallel axis theorem,

$= M\left[\dfrac{2}{5} \times {5}^{2} + {10}^{2}\right]$

$= M [ 110 ] = M{k}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \sqrt{110}cm$

Therefore, $x = 110$.

questions.q: Four identical discs each of mass '$M$' and diameter '$a$' are arranged in a small plane as shown in figure. If the moment of inertia of the system about $O{O}^{'}$ is $\dfrac{x}{4}M{a}^{2}$. Then, the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
Considering four identical discs as $1, 2, 3$ and $4$.

Moment of inertia of disc about diagonal is ${I}_{1} = {I}_{3} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4}$

Now using parallel axis theorem,

Moment of inertia of disc $2$ and $4$ is

${I}_{2} = {I}_{4} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4} + M{R}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}M{R}^{2}$

So, net moment of inertia about $O{O}^{'}$ is

$I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + {I}_{3} + {I}_{4}$

$= 2\left(\dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4}\right) + 2\left(\dfrac{5}{4}M{R}^{2}\right)$

$= \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2}M{R}^{2}$= 3M{R}^{2}$

Putting $R = \dfrac{a}{2}$

$I = \dfrac{3M{a}^{2}}{4}$, so,$x = 3$

questions.q:
A solid cylinder length is suspended symmetrically through two massless strings, as shown in the figure. The distance from the initial rest position, the cylinder should be unbinding the strings to achieve a speed of $4m{s}^{- 1}$, is _____$cm$.

(take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
The portion of the strings between the ceiling and the cylinder are at rest. Hence, the points of the cylinder where the strings leave it are at rest. The cylinder is thus rolling without slipping on the strings.

Now, from energy conservation

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

where, $I$ is moment of inertia of cylinder and $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$ is angular velocity.

Then, we have

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2}{\omega}^{2} ⇒ gh = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{R}^{2}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2}$

$10h = \dfrac{16}{2} + \dfrac{16}{4} ⇒ h = 1 . 2m = 120cm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pulley of radius $1 . 5m$ is rotated about its axis by a force $F = \left(12t - 3{t}^{2}\right)N$ applied tangentially (while $t$ is measured in seconds). If moment of inertia of the pulley about its axis of rotation is $4 . 5kg{m}^{2}$, the number of rotations made by the pulley before its direction of motion is reversed, will be $\dfrac{K}{\pi}$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Torque of pulley about its axis is $τ = I\alpha$, where, $I$ is moment of inertia and $\alpha$ is angular acceleration.

Torque of a force about its axis is $τ = FR$, here, $R$ is radius of pulley.

Then, $\left(12t - 3{t}^{2}\right)1 . 5 = 4 . 5\alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = 4t - {t}^{2}$

Angular acceleration in terms of angular velocity is

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{d \omega}{d t} = 4t - {t}^{2}$

$⇒ \omega = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(4t - {t}^{2}\right) d t$

$⇒ \omega = 2{t}^{2} - \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3}$

For $\omega = 0, 2{t}^{2} - \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3} = 0 ⇒ {t}^{2}\left(2 - \dfrac{t}{3}\right) = 0$

$⇒ t = 0\text{or}6s$

Now, using $\omega = \dfrac{d \theta}{d t}$, we have

$\dfrac{d \theta}{d t} = 2{t}^{2} - \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3} ⇒ \theta = {∫}_{0}^{6}\left(2{t}^{2} - \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3}\right) d t$

$= {\left[\dfrac{2{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{{t}^{4}}{12}\right]}_{0}^{6}$

$= {6}^{3}\left(\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{6}{12}\right) = {6}^{3}\left(\dfrac{8 - 6}{12}\right)= \dfrac{{6}^{3}}{6} = 36$

Number of revolutions $= \dfrac{36}{2\pi} = \dfrac{18}{\pi}$

$∴ K = 18$

questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the rod about an axis perpendicular to its length and passing through the centre is $I = \dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{12}$.

questions.q: A disc of mass $1kg$ and radius $R$ is free of rotate about a horizontal axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc. A body of same mass as that of disc is fixed at the highest point of the disc. Now the system is released, when the body comes to the lowest position, its angular speed will be $4\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3R}}rad{s}^{- 1}$ where $x =$ _____ .
questions.solution:
Let the angular speed of disc be $\omega$.

Using conservation of mechanical energy

$mg2R = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{disc}{\omega}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{particle}{\omega}^{2}$

Where, $I$ is moment of inertia.

$⇒ mg2R = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2}}{2}\left[\dfrac{{m}^{2}}{2} + m{R}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ mg2R = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2}}{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}m{R}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{4}{\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{2g}{R}$

$⇒ {\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{8g}{3R}$

Thus, angular speed is $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{80}{3R}}rad{s}^{- 1}$

Given $\omega = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3R}}$

Comparing both, $16\dfrac{x}{3R} = \dfrac{80}{3R}$

Therefore, the value of $x = 5$.

questions.q: A solid cylinder and a solid sphere, having same mass $M$ and radius $R$, roll down the same inclined plane from top without slipping. They start from rest. The ratio of velocity of the solid cylinder to that of the solid sphere, with which they reach the ground, will be
questions.solution:
During pure rolling, the work done by the friction is zero. Therefore, we can apply conservation of mechanical energy.

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(m + \dfrac{I}{{R}^{2}}\right){v}^{2}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1 + \dfrac{I}{m{R}^{2}}}}$

For a solid cylinder $\dfrac{I}{m{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and for a solid sphere, $\dfrac{I}{m{R}^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$\dfrac{{v}_{Cyl}}{{v}_{Sph}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{2}{5}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}}}$= \sqrt{\dfrac{14}{15}}$

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one end is ${I}_{1}$. The same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about a diameter is ${I}_{2}$. If $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}$ is $\dfrac{x{\pi}^{2}}{3}$, then the value of $x$ will be ______.
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of rod rotating about an axis passing through one end is ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{3} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Moment of inertia of ring rotating about one of its diameters is ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2}$.

Since the rod is bent into a ring, the circumference of the ring and the length of the rod are equal, $l = 2\piR$

Then, ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{8{\pi}^{2}}$

Thus, the ratio $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{8{\pi}^{2}}{3}$, so $x = 8$.

Angular momentum of a rotating and translating body is given by,

${L}_{O} = mvR + I\omega = mvR + \dfrac{2}{3}M{R}^{2}\omega$

For rolling, $v = \omegaR$

$⇒ {L}_{O} = m\omega{R}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}m\omega{R}^{2}$

Therefore, the value of $a = 5$.

A $\sqrt{34}m$ long ladder weighing $10kg$ leans on a frictionless wall. Its feet rest on the floor $3m$ away from the wall as shown in the figure. If ${F}_{f}$ and ${F}_{w}$ are the reaction forces of the floor and the wall, then ratio of $\dfrac{{F}_{w}}{{F}_{f}}$ will be :

questions.q:
A uniform disc with mass $M = 4kg$ and radius $R = 10cm$ is mounted on a fixed horizontal axle as shown in figure. A block with mass $m = 2kg$ hangs from a massless cord that is wrapped around the rim of the disc. During the fall of the block, the cord does not slip and there is no friction at the axle. The tension in the cord is _____ $N$.

(Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Let $a$ be the acceleration of block and $\alpha$ be the angular acceleration of disc.

Now, for unwrapping without slipping, $R\alpha = a$.

Forces acting on block are shown in FDB.

Using Newton's second law

$mg - T = ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Torque about centre of disc is $τ = Ia$

$TR = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = \dfrac{4{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = ⇒ T = 2R\alpha . . . \left(2\right)$

Putting the value of tension in equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

$mg - 2R\alpha = ma ⇒ mg - 2R\dfrac{a}{R} = ma ⇒ mg - 2a = ma ⇒ ma + 2a = mg ⇒ a = \dfrac{mg}{m + 2} = \dfrac{2 \times 10}{2 + 2} = 5m{s}^{- 2}$

Now, $\alpha = \dfrac{5}{0 . 1} = 50rad{s}^{- 2}$

Tension in the cord is $T = 2 \times 0 . 1 \times 50 =$10N$.

$2{I}_{1} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}\left\{∵ {I}_{com} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}\right\}$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4} ⇒ D \to III$

questions.q: A solid spherical ball is rolling on a frictionless horizontal plane surface about its axis of symmetry. The ratio of rotational kinetic energy of the ball to its total kinetic energy is
questions.solution:
Under pure rolling condition: $v = \omegaR$

Translational $K . E = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Rotational $K . E = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5}m{R}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{5}m{v}^{2}$

Total $K . E = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{5}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{7}{10}m{v}^{2}$

So, $\dfrac{RotationalK \cdot E}{TotalK \cdot E} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{5}m{v}^{2}}{\dfrac{7}{10}m{v}^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{7}$

questions.q: A thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating with a constant angular velocity $2rad{s}^{- 1}$ in a horizontal plane about an axis vertical to its plane and passing through the center of the ring. If two objects each of mass $m$ be attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of ring, the ring will then rotate with an angular velocity (in $rad{s}^{- 1}$).
questions.solution:
As the masses are gently placed we can apply conservation of angular momentum.

Initial moment of Inertia ${I}_{1} = M{R}^{2}$

Final moment of inertia ${I}_{2} = M{R}^{2} + \left(2m\right){R}^{2}$

By conservation of angular momentum

${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} = {I}_{2}{\omega}_{2}$⇒ M{R}^{2} \times 2 = \left(M + 2m\right){R}^{2} \times {\omega}_{2}$

$⇒ {\omega}_{2} = \dfrac{2M}{M + 2m}rad{s}^{- 1}$

Moment of Inertia (M.I.) of four bodies having same mass $M$ and radius $2R$ are as follows
${I}_{1} =$ M.I. of solid sphere about its diameter
${I}_{2} =$ M.I. of solid cylinder about its axis
${I}_{3} =$ M.I. of solid circular disc about its diameter
${I}_{4} =$ M.I. of thin circular ring about its diameter
If $2\left({I}_{2} + {I}_{3}\right) + {I}_{4} = x{I}_{1}$ then the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
$∵ 2\left({I}_{2} + {I}_{3}\right) + {I}_{4} = x{I}_{1}$

Now

For solid sphere about its diameter ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}$,

For solid cylinder about its axis ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}$,

For circular disc about its diameter ${I}_{3} = \dfrac{1}{4}M{R}^{2}$

And for circular ring about its diameter ${I}_{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4}\right) + \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ 2 = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ x = 5$

questions.solution:
Torque in vector form is expressed as vector multiplication of position vector and force.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{τ} = \left(- 10\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)Nm$

questions.q: A fly wheel is accelerated uniformly from rest and rotates through $5rad$ in the first second. The angle rotated by the fly wheel in the next second, will be :
questions.solution:
Here the angular acceleration is constant, so we have,

$\theta = \omegat + \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha{t}^{2}$.

When flywheel is rotated from rest in the first second, then ${\theta}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha{\left(1\right)}^{2} = 5rad$

$⇒ \alpha = 10rad{s}^{- 2}$

The angle turned by flywheel in the next second is ${\theta}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha{\left(2\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(10\right)\left(4\right) = 20rad{s}^{- 2}$

Thus, the angle turned during next second is $\theta = 20 - 5 = 15rad$

questions.q: A solid disc of radius $20cm$ and mass $10kg$ is rotating with an angular velocity of $600rpm$, about an axis normal to its circular plane and passing through its centre of mass. The retarding torque required to bring the disc at rest in $10s$ is _________$\pi \times {10}^{- 1}Nm$
questions.solution:
$τ = \dfrac{\DeltaL}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{I\left({\omega}_{f} - {\omega}_{i}\right)}{\Deltat}$

$τ = \dfrac{\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2} \times [ 0 - \omega ]}{\Deltat}$

$= \dfrac{10 \times {\left(20 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2}}{2} \times \dfrac{600 \times \pi}{30 \times 10}$

$= 0 . 4\pi = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 1}$

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Moment of inertia of a circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about $X, Y$ axes (passing through its plane) and Z-axis which is perpendicular to its plane were found to be ${I}_{x}, {I}_{y}$ and ${I}_{z}$, respectively. The respective radii of gyration about all the three axes will be the same.

Reason R: A rigid body making rotational motion has fixed mass and shape. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.

Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A.
questions.solution:
${I}_{z} = {I}_{x} + {I}_{y}$ (using perpendicular axis theorem)

and $I = m{k}^{2} ( K:$ radius of gyration)

so $m{K}_{z}^{2} = m{K}_{x}^{2} + m{K}_{y}^{2}$

${K}_{z}^{2} = {K}_{x}^{2} + {K}_{y}^{2}$

So radius of gyration about axes $x, y$ and $z$ will not be same, hence assertion A is not correct reason R is correct statement (property of a rigid body).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle of mass $m$ is moving in time $t$ on a trajectory given by,

$\overset{\to}{r} = 10\alpha{t}^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\left(t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are dimensional constants.

The angular momentum of the particle becomes the same as it was for $t = 0$ at time $t =$_____ seconds.
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{r} = 10\alpha{t}^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\left(t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{v} = 20\alpha + \overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{L} = m\left(\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{v}\right)$

$= m\left[10\alpha{t}^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\left(t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}\right] \times \left[20\alpha\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\overset{^}{j}\right]$

$\overset{\to}{L} = m\left[50\alpha\beta{t}^{2}\overset{^}{k} - 100\alpha\beta\left({t}^{2} - 5t\right)\overset{^}{k}\right]$

At $t = 0, \overset{\to}{L} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$50\alpha\beta{t}^{2} - 100\alpha\beta\left({t}^{2} - 5t\right) = 0$

$t - 2\left(t - 5\right) = 0$

$t = 10sec$

Now, $\dfrac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$
$⇒ x = 2$

A solid cylinder of mass $m$ is wrapped with an inextensible light string and, is placed on a rough inclined plane as shown in the figure. The frictional force acting between the cylinder and the inclined plane is:

[The coefficient of static friction, ${\mu}_{s}$, is $0 . 4$ ]
questions.solution:
Let's take solid cylinder is in equilibrium

$T + f = mgsin60$

$TR - fR = 0$

Solving we get

$T = {f}_{req} = \dfrac{mgsin\theta}{2}$

But limiting friction $<$ required friction

$\mumgcos60 ° < \dfrac{mg sin60 °}{2}$

$∴$ Hence cylinder will not remain in equilibrium

Hence $f =$ kinetic

$= {\mu}_{k}N$

$= {\mu}_{k}mgcos60 °$

$= \dfrac{mg}{5}$

A force $\overset{\to}{F} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ is applied on an intersection point of $x = 2$ plane and $x$-axis. The magnitude of torque of this force about a point $\left(2, 3, 4\right)$ is ________.

(Round off to the Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F}$

$\overset{\to}{r} = \left(2\overset{^}{i}\right) - \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

and $\overset{\to}{F} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & - 3 & - 4 \\ 4 & 3 & 4\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(- 12 + 12\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(0 + 16\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(0 + 12\right)$

$= - 16\overset{^}{i} + 12\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ | \overset{\to}{τ} | = \sqrt{{16}^{2} + {12}^{2}} = 20$

questions.q: A sphere of radius $a$ and mass $m$ rolls along a horizontal plane with constant speed ${v}_{0}$. It encounters an inclined plane at angle $\theta$ and climbs upward. Assuming that it rolls without slipping, how far up the sphere will travel?
questions.solution:
From energy conservation
$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}_{0}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I \omega}^{2}$
$⇒ mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}_{0}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5}{ma}^{2} \times {v}_{0}^{2}{a}^{2}$
$⇒ gh = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}_{0}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{5}{v}_{0}^{2}$
$⇒ gh = \dfrac{7}{10}{v}_{0}^{2}$

From triangle, $sin\theta = \dfrac{h}{l}$
Then $h = lsin\theta$
$⇒ lsin\theta = \dfrac{7}{10}{v}_{0}^{2}g$
Thus, the sphere will travel distance, $l = \dfrac{7}{10}\dfrac{{{v}_{0}}^{2}}{gsin\theta}$.

questions.q: The linear mass density of a thin rod $AB$ of length $L$ varies from $A$ to $B$ as $\lambda\left(x\right) = {\lambda}_{0}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{L}\right)$, where $x$ is the distance from $A$. If $M$ is the mass of the rod then its moment of inertia about an axis passing through $A$ and perpendicular to the rod :
questions.solution:
$dm = \lambda . dv$

$dI = dm . {x}^{2}$

$= {\lambda}_{0}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{L}\right) . {x}^{2}dx$

$I = {\lambda}_{0}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left({x}^{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{L}\right)dx$

$= {\lambda}_{0}{\left|\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{{x}_{4}}{4L}\right|}_{0}^{L}$

$= {\lambda}_{0}\left[\dfrac{{L}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{{L}_{3}}{4}\right]$

$I = \dfrac{7{\lambda}_{0}{L}^{3}}{12}$

$m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{L}\lambda dx = \dfrac{3{\lambda}_{0}L}{2}$

$\dfrac{I}{m} = \dfrac{7{L}^{2}}{12 \times \dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{7{L}^{2}}{18}$

$⇒$I = \dfrac{7}{18}{mL}^{2}$

questions.q: A wheel is rotating freely with an angular speed $\omega$ on a shaft. The moment of inertia of the wheel is $I$ and the moment of inertia of the shaft is negligible. Another wheel of moment of inertia $3I$ initially at rest is suddenly coupled to the same shaft. The resultant fractional loss in the kinetic energy of the system is:
questions.solution:
From angular momentum conservation
$I\omega + 0 = I{\omega}_{C} + 3I{\omega}_{C}$
$\omegac = \dfrac{\omega}{4}$

Loss of kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} ( I + 3I ) {\left(\dfrac{\omega}{4}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}I\dfrac{{\omega}^{2}}{4}$

$= \dfrac{3}{8}I{\omega}^{2}$

Fractional loss $= \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: For a uniform rectangular sheet shown in the figure, the ratio of moments of inertia about the axes perpendicular to the sheet and passing through $O$ (the centre of mass) and $O$' (corner point) is:
questions.solution:
We will use Parallel Axes Theorem here,

Distance between $O{O}^{'}$ is,

$O{O}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{4}}$

So, according to parallel axis theorem we have,

$\dfrac{{I}_{O}}{I{O}^{'}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{12}\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{M}{12}\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right) + M\left(\dfrac{{a}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{4}\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{12}\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{M}{3}\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.q: A circular disc of mass $\text{M}$ and radius $\text{R}$ is rotating about its axis with angular speed ${ω}_{1}$. If another stationary disc having radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and same mass $\text{M}$ is dropped co-axially on to the rotating disc. Gradually both discs attain constant angular speed ${ω}_{2}$. The energy lost in the process is $\text{p%}$ of the initial energy. Value of $p$ is ______
questions.solution:
${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} + {I}_{2}{\omega}_{2} = \left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right) \times {\omega}_{f}$

$\dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{2} \times \omega + 0\left(\dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{8}\right)\dfrac{16}{25}$

${\omega}_{f} = \dfrac{4}{5}\omega$

Final $K . E$., ${K}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{8}\right)\dfrac{16}{25}{\omega}^{2}$

${K}_{f} = \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{5}$ ; ${K}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{2}\right){\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{4}$

Percentage loss in kinetic energy $% loss = \dfrac{\dfrac{{MR}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{5}}{\dfrac{{MR}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{4}} \times 100 = 20 %$

questions.q: Moment of inertia of a cylinder of mass $m,$ length $L$ and radius $R$ about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the axis of the cylinder is $I = M\left(\dfrac{{R}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{L}^{2}}{12}\right) .$ If such a cylinder is to be made for a given mass of a material, the ratio $\dfrac{L}{R}$ for it to have minimum possible $I$ is:
questions.solution:
Let a cylinder of mass ${m}_{1}$, length $L$ and radius $R$ then take elementary disc of radius $R$ and trickiness $dx$ at distance of $x$ from axis $OO '$ then moment of inertia about $OO '$ as this element

$dl = \dfrac{{dmR}^{2}}{4} + {dmx}^{2}$

$I = ∫ dl = ∫ \dfrac{{dmR}^{2}}{4} + {∫}_{n = L / 2}^{n = - L / 2}\dfrac{M}{L}dx \times {x}^{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{MR}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{ML}^{2}}{12}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{M}{4} \times \dfrac{V}{\pi L} + \dfrac{{ML}^{2}}{12}$

$\dfrac{dI}{dL} = - \dfrac{mV}{4{\pi L}^{2}} + \dfrac{M \times 2L}{12} = 0$

$⇒ V = \dfrac{2}{3}{\pi L}^{3} ⇒ {\pi R}^{2}L = \dfrac{2}{3}{\pi L}^{3} ⇒ \dfrac{L}{R} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$\left(I = \dfrac{MV}{4\pi L} + \dfrac{{ML}^{2}}{12}\right)$

questions.q: A block of mass $m = 1kg$ slides with velocity $v = 6m{s}^{- 1}$ on a frictionless horizontal surface and collides with a uniform vertical rod and sticks to it as shown. The rod is pivoted about $O$ and swings as a result of the collision making angle $\theta$ before momentarily coming to rest. if the rod has mass $M = 2kg,$ and length $ℓ = 1m,$ the value of $\theta$ is approximately$\left( takeg = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Angular momentum

$mvl = \left(m{l}^{2} + \dfrac{2m{l}^{2}}{3}\right)\omega$

$mvl = \dfrac{5}{3}m{l}^{2}\omega$

$\omega = \dfrac{3v}{5l}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}{I \omega}^{2} = 2mg\dfrac{l}{2}\left(1 - cos\theta\right) + mgl\left(1 - cos\theta\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{5}{3}m{l}^{2}\right)\dfrac{9{v}^{2}}{25{l}^{2}} = 2mgl\left(1 - cos\theta\right)$

$\dfrac{3}{5 \times 2}{mv}^{2} = 2mgl\left(1 - cos \theta\right)$

$\dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{36}{2 \times 10} = 1 - cos\theta$

$1 - \dfrac{27}{50} = cos\theta$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{23}{50} = 0 . 46$

$\theta = \cos^{- 1}\left(0 . 46\right) = 63 °$

$\left(80 + \dfrac{200}{2}\right) \times 5 = \dfrac{200}{2}\omega '$

$\omega ' = 9rev / sec .

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a bob of mass $m$ is tied to a massless string whose other end portion is wound on a fly wheel (disc) of radius $r$ and mass $m .$ When released from rest the bob starts falling vertically. When it has covered a distance of $h,$ the angular speed of the wheel will be:
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I \omega}^{2}$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}{m \omega}^{2}{r}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{mr}^{2}}{2}{\omega}^{2}$ ( since $I = \dfrac{{mr}^{2}}{2}$ and $v = r \omega$ )

$mgh = \dfrac{3}{4}{m \omega}^{2}{r}^{2}$

Hence, $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3{r}^{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{r}\sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person of mass $M$ is sitting on a swing of length $L$ and swinging with and an angular amplitude ${\theta}_{0} .$ If the person stands up when the swing passes through its lowest point, the work done by him, assuming that his centre of mass moves by a distance $l\left(l < < L\right),$ is close to:
questions.solution:
From angular momentum conservation
$\begin{array}{ll}M{V}_{0}L = MV ( L - l ) \\ V = {V}_{0}\left(\dfrac{L}{L - l}\right)\end{array}$
Now
$W = Mgl + \dfrac{1}{2}M\left[{{V}_{0}}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{L}{L - l}\right)}^{2} - {{V}_{0}}^{2}\right]$
Since $l ≪ L$
$\begin{array}{ll}W = Mgl + \dfrac{1}{2}M\left[{{V}_{0}}^{2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{l}{L}\right)}^{- 2} - {{V}_{0}}^{2}\right] \\ = Mgl + \dfrac{1}{2}M\left[{{V}_{0}}^{2}\left(1 + 2\dfrac{l}{L}\right) - {{V}_{0}}^{2}\right] \\ = Mgl + M\left[{{V}_{0}}^{2}\left(\dfrac{l}{L}\right)\right]\end{array}$
From SHM
${V}_{0} = \omegaA = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{L}} \times L{\theta}_{0} = \sqrt{gL}{\theta}_{0}$
Using this
$\begin{array}{ll}W = Mgl + M\left[gL \times {{\theta}_{0}}^{2} \times \left(\dfrac{l}{L}\right)\right] \\ W = Mgl\left[1 + {{\theta}_{0}}^{2}\right]\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rod of length $l$ is being rotated in a horizontal plane with a constant angular speed about an axis passing through one of its ends. If the tension generated in the rod due to rotation is $T ( x )$ at a distance $x$ from the axis, then which of the following graphs depicts it most closely?
questions.solution:
The mass of the rod at a distance $x$ from the axis is $dm = \dfrac{M}{L} . dx$
$T = ( dm ) {\omega}^{2}x$

Integrating the above equation from $x$ to $L$
$= {∫}_{x}^{L}\dfrac{M}{L}{\omega}^{2}xdx$
$= \dfrac{M}{L}{\omega}^{2}{\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{x}^{L}$
$\dfrac{M}{2L}{\omega}^{2}\left[{L}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right]$
The above equation depicts the relation between tension and length of rod as downward opening parabola.

questions.q: A circular disc of radius $b$ has a hole of radius $a$ at its centre(see figure). If the mass per unit area of the disc varies as $\left(\dfrac{{\sigma}_{0}}{r}\right)$ then, the radius of gyration of the disc about its axis passing through the center is
questions.solution:
Solution: (B)
$dm = \sigma2\pirdr$
$= \dfrac{{\sigma}_{0}}{r}2\pirdr$
$m =2 \pi{\sigma}_{0}{∫}_{a}^{b}dr = 2\pi{\sigma}_{0} ( b - a )$

$I = 2\pi{\sigma}_{0}{∫}_{a}^{b}{r}^{2}dr = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi{\sigma}_{0}\left({b}^{3} - {a}^{3}\right)$
Radius of gyration $= \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{3}\pi{\sigma}_{0}\left({b}^{3} - {a}^{3}\right)}{2\pi{\sigma}_{0}\left(b - a\right)}}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{{b}^{3} - {a}^{3}}{3 ( b - a )}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{( b - a ) ( {b}^{2} + {a}^{2} + ab )}{3 ( b - a )}}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{{b}^{2} + {a}^{2} + ab}{3}}$.

$I = 2\pi{\sigma}_{0}{∫}_{a}^{b}{r}^{2}dr = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi{\sigma}_{0}\left({b}^{3} - {a}^{3}\right)$

Moment of inertia of disc about the axis passing its centre and perpendicular to its surface, ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{7M}{8}\right){\left(2R\right)}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{7M{R}^{2}}{4}$.

$\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{7}{4} \times \dfrac{80}{1} = 140$

questions.q: The time dependence of the position of a particle of mass $m = 2$ is given by $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = 2t\overset{^}{i} - 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$ . Its angular momentum, with respect to the origin, at time $t = 2$ is:
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{r} = 2t\overset{^}{i} - 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{\to}{v} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 6t\overset{^}{j}$
Momentum $\overset{\to}{p} = m\overset{\to}{v}$
$= 4\overset{^}{i} - 12t\overset{^}{j}$
$∴$ angular momentum $\overset{\to}{L} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{p}$
$= \left(2t\overset{^}{i} - 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) \times \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 12t\overset{^}{j}\right)$
$= - 24{t}^{2}\overset{^}{k} + 12{t}^{2}\overset{^}{k}$
$= - 12{t}^{2}\overset{^}{k}$
At time $t = 2$
$\overset{\to}{L} = - 48\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: A thin disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ has mass per unit area $\sigma\left(r\right) = k{r}^{2}$ where $r$ is the distance from its centre. Its moment inertia about an axis going through its centre of mass and perpendicular to its plane is:
questions.solution:
$dm = \sigma ⋅ dA = \sigma2\pirdr$
$= 2\pik{r}^{3}dr$
$M = ∫ dm = 2\pik\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{r}^{3}dr$
$= 2\pik\left(\dfrac{{R}^{4}}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pik{R}^{4}}{2}$
$dI = dm{r}^{2} = 2\pik{r}^{5}dr$
$I = 2\pik\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{r}^{5}dr = 2\pik\dfrac{{R}^{6}}{6} = \dfrac{2\pik{R}^{6}}{3 \times 2}$

since, $\text{M} = \dfrac{{\pi kR}^{4}}{2}$

so,
$I = \dfrac{2M{R}^{2}}{3}$

questions.q: Two coaxial discs, having moments of inertia {I}_{1} and $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2}$ , are rotating with respective angular velocities ${\omega}_{1} and \dfrac{{\omega}_{1}}{2}$ , about their common axis. They are brought in contact with each other and thereafter they rotate with a common angular velocity. If ${E}_{f} and {E}_{i}$ are the final and initial total energies, then $\left({E}_{f} - {E}_{i}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
As external torque is zero, angular momentum remains conserved.
${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} + \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2}\dfrac{{\omega}_{1}}{2} = \left({I}_{1} + \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2}\right)\omega$
$∴$ Common angular velocity $\omega = \dfrac{5{\omega}_{1}}{6}$
$∴${E}_{f} - {E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left({I}_{1} + \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2}\right){\omega}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times {I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}{}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{{I}_{l}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{{\omega}_{1}}{2}\right)}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3{I}_{1}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{5}{6}{\omega}_{1}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{9}{16}{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{75{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2} - 81{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2}}{144}$
$= - \dfrac{6{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2}}{144}$
$= - \dfrac{{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2}}{24}$

questions.q: A thin smooth rod of length $L$ and mass $M$ is rotating freely with angular speed ${\omega}_{0}$ about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through center. Two beads of mass $m$ and negligible size are at the center of the rod initially. The beads of mass $m$ and negligible size are at the center of the rod initially. The beads are free to slide along the rod. The angular speed of the system, when the beads reach the opposite ends of the rod, will be:
questions.solution:
From conservation of angular momentum.
$\dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{12}{\omega}_{0} = \left[\dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{12} + m{\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}^{2} + m{\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}^{2}\right]\omega'$
$\dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{12}{\omega}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{12} + \dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{2}\right)\omega'$
$\omega' = \dfrac{M{\omega}_{0}}{M + 6m}$

questions.q: A stationary horizontal disc is free to rotate about its axis. When a torque is applied on it, its kinetic energy as a function of $\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle by which it has rotated, is given as $k{\theta}^{2}$. If its moment of inertia is $I$ then the angular acceleration of the disc is:
questions.solution:
Kinetic Energy $= k{\theta}^{2}$
$\dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} = k{\theta}^{2}$
${\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{2k{\theta}^{2}}{I}$
Differentiate both side w.r.t. $\theta$ .
$2\omega\dfrac{d\omega}{d\theta} = \dfrac{4k\theta}{I}$
$\omega\dfrac{d\omega}{d\theta} = \dfrac{2k\theta}{I}$
$\alpha = \dfrac{2k\theta}{I}$

questions.q: A rectangular solid box of length $0.3m$ is held horizontally, with one of its sides on the edge of a platform of height $5m$ . When released, it slips off the table in a very short time $τ = 0.01s$ , remaining essentially horizontal. The angle by which it would rotate when it hits the ground will be (in radians) close to:
questions.solution:
Angular impulse = change in angular momentum
$τ\Deltat = \DeltaL$
$mg\dfrac{l}{2} \times 0.01 = \dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{3}\omega$
$\omega = \dfrac{3g \times 0.01}{2l} = \dfrac{3 \times 10 \times 0.01}{2 \times 0.3} = 0.5rad / sec$
Time taken by rod to hit the ground = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 5}{10}} = 1s$
Angle rotated by rod = $\omegat = 0.5 \times 1 = 0.5rad$

questions.q: A solid sphere and solid cylinder of identical radii approach an incline with the same linear velocity (see figure). Both roll without slipping all throughout. The two climb maximum heights ${h}_{sph}$ and ${h}_{cyl}$ on the inline. The ratio $\dfrac{{h}_{sph}}{{h}_{cyl}}$ is given by:
questions.solution:
From conservation of mechanical energy,
For solid sphere: $\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{sph}{V}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{sph}{\omega}^{2} = {m}_{sph}g{h}_{sph}$
$\dfrac{{V}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{5} = g{h}_{sph}$
$\dfrac{7{V}^{2}}{10} = g{h}_{sph}$ …(i)
For cylinder: $\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{cyl}{V}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{cyl}{\omega}^{2} = {m}_{cyl}g{h}_{cyl}$
$\dfrac{{V}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{4} = g{h}_{cyl}$
$\dfrac{3{V}^{2}}{4} = g{h}_{cyl}$ …(ii)
From (i) and (ii) $\dfrac{{h}_{sph}}{{h}_{cyl}} = \dfrac{14}{15}$

When cylinder is rotated, water will rise at the edge and will dip at the centre. The difference in pressure at $A$ and $O$ is ${P}_{A} - {P}_{0} = ρgh .$ Due to height difference.

pressure difference ${P}_{1} - {P}_{0} = ρ ⋅ {a}_{cm}R$ Due to rotation.

$= ρ ⋅ \left({\omega}^{2} . \dfrac{R}{2}\right)R$



$∴ ρgh = ρ\dfrac{{\omega}^{2}{R}^{2}}{2} ⇒ h = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2} ⋅ {R}^{2}}{2g} = {\left(2\pi \times 2\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{{\left(0.05\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 10}$

$= 0.02m$

$= 2cm$

questions.q: A rod of length $50cm$ is pivoted at one end. It is raised such that it makes an angle of ${30}^{o}$ from the horizontal as shown and released from rest. Its angular speed when it passes through the horizontal (in $rad{s}^{- 1}$ ) will be $\left(g = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$

From conservation of mechanical energy


Loss in gravitational $PE =$ gain in $KE$

$mg\dfrac{l}{2}sin ⁡ {30}^{o} = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$mg\dfrac{l}{2}sin ⁡ {30}^{o} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{3}{\omega}^{2}$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{2l}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 10}{2 \times 50 \times {10}^{- 2}}} = \sqrt{30}rad / s$

$⇒ \theta = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.q: From a uniform circular disc of radius R and mass 9 M, a small disc of radius $\dfrac{R}{3}$ is removed as shown in the figure. The moment of inertia of the remaining disc about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the disc and passing through centre of disc is:
questions.solution:
By parallel axis theorem,

Mass of smaller disc $= \dfrac{9M}{\pi{R}^{2}} \pi{( \dfrac{R}{3} )}^{2} = M$

MI of smaller disc $= \dfrac{M{\left(\dfrac{R}{3}\right)}^{2}}{2} + M{\left(\dfrac{2R}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$MI = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{18} + \dfrac{4M{R}^{2}}{9}$

$MI = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}$

$MI = MI\left(Bigger\right) - MI\left(Smaller\right)$

$= \dfrac{9M{R}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}$

$= 4M{R}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a physical balance working on the principle of moments, when $5mg$ weight is placed on the left pan, the beam becomes horizontal. Both the empty pans of the balance are of equal mass. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Every object that is weighed using this balance appears lighter than its actual weight
Left arm is shorter than the right arm
Both the arms are of same length
Left arm is longer than the right arm
questions.solution:
Let ${m}_{1} and {m}_{2}$ be the masses of pan

It is given that ${m}_{1} = {m}_{2}$



Since balance is achieved, so net torque about $O$ should be zero.
$\left(5mg + {m}_{1} g\right){r}_{1} = \left({m}_{2} g\right){r}_{2}$
$⇒ \left(5mg + {m}_{1}g\right){r}_{1} = \left({m}_{1}g\right){r}_{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{{m}_{1}g}{{m}_{1}g + 5mg}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} < 1$

So, left arm is shorter than the right arm.

$m = ρ\left(\pi{R}^{2}l\right) . . . ( 1 )$

$dm = ρ\pi\left(2R . dRl + {R}^{2}dl\right)$

$0 = ρ\pi\left(2RldR + {R}^{2}dl\right)$

$2RldR = - {R}^{2}dl . . . ( 2 )$

$I = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{M{l}^{2}}{12}$

Conservation of angular momentum about point $O$,

If the angular speed of the particle is $12rad{s}^{- 1}$ , the magnitude of its angular momentum about a point on the ground right under the center of the circle is:
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{p} = mv\overset{^}{j} = 2 \times v\overset{^}{j} = 2 \times 0 .6 \times 12 = 7 .2 \times 2 = 14 .4 \overset{^}{j} \left(v = r$\omega\right)

$\overset{→}{r} = ( 0 .8 \overset{^}{k} + 0 .6 \overset{^}{i} )⇒ \overset{→}{L} = \overset{→}{r} $\times \overset{→}{p}

$= \left(0 .6 \overset{^}{i} + 0 .8 \overset{^}{k}\right) \times$14 .4 \overset{^}{j}$

$= 0 .6 $\times$14 .4 \overset{^}{k} - 0 .8 $\times$14 .4 \overset{^}{i}$

$= 14.4 $\left(0.6\overset{^}{k} - 0.8\overset{^}{i}\right)$

$⇒ | \overset{→}{L} |= 14.4\sqrt{{\left(0.6\right)}^{2} + {\left(0.8\right)}^{2}}$

$= 14.4\sqrt{0.36 + 0.64}$

$= 14.4 \times 1$

$= 14.4kgm^{2}s^{- 1}$
